def decide(bars, account):
    """Hold while close is above a rising 50-day average; exit after 3 closes below it."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = len(closes)
    if n < 55:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 50-day average"
    avg_now = sum(closes[-50:]) / 50
    avg_prev = sum(closes[-55:-5]) / 50
    price = closes[-1]
    rising = avg_now > avg_prev
    if account["position"] <= 0:
        if price > avg_now and rising:
            return "BUY", "close above a rising 50-day average"
        return "HOLD", "no entry signal"
    below = 0
    for i in range(1, 4):
        if closes[-i] < sum(closes[-i - 49:len(closes) - i + 1]) / 50:
            below += 1
        else:
            break
    if below >= 3:
        return "SELL", "close below the 50-day average for 3 days"
    return "HOLD", "uptrend intact"

Starting strategy supplied by the researcher and identical for every run; you did not write it. It is deliberately simple. Judge it on the evidence like any other version.
def decide(bars, account):
    """Seed strategy: hold the stock while its close is above the 20-day average."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    if len(closes) < 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 20-day average"
    average = sum(closes[-20:]) / 20
    price = closes[-1]
    if account["position"] <= 0 and price > average:
        return "BUY", "close is above the 20-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and price < average:
        return "SELL", "close is below the 20-day average"
    return "HOLD", "no change"
